the cysteine-desulfhydrase activity found in the two bacteria studied is not a cystathionase, but a true desulfhydrase.
the desulfhydrase of S. typhi murium is an enzyme different from the cysteine aminotransferase and from the cystathione β-synthase.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S. typhmurium possesses a cysteine desuffhydrase activity which is different from the activity of the catabolic pathway of cysteine, while E. coli does not.
S. typhmurium has a cysteine desulphhydrase activity which is inducible by both cysteine or glucose, while in E. coli the activity is only inducible by glucose and is repressed by glucose.
cysteine desulphhydrase activity in S. typhumurium and E. coli is inducible, but not catabolite-repressible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cysteine desulphhydrase activity of both S. typhymurium and E. coli are inducible.
